memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: You must destroy all the peoples the Lord your God gives over to you. Do not look on them with pity and do not serve their gods, for that will be a snare to you. You may say to yourselves, "These nations are stronger than we are. How can we drive them out?" But do not be afraid of them; remember well what the Lord your God did to Pharaoh and to all Egypt. - Deut 7:16-18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God knew His people would look at the powerful nations ahead and feel their knees buckle. "These nations are stronger than we are. How can we drive them out?" Fear whispers that the obstacle is too big and we are too small. But God's answer is not to deny the difficulty; it is to redirect their gaze. "Remember well what the Lord your God did to Pharaoh." The cure for fear is not pretending the challenge is small, but remembering how great our God is.

Fear grows when we stare at the size of our problems and forget the greatness of our God. Israel had watched God shatter the most powerful empire on earth to set them free. If God could bring Egypt to its knees, surely He could handle the nations of Canaan. Remembering His past faithfulness is fuel for present courage.

We battle the same fearful whisper. The challenges before us — the diagnosis, the broken relationship, the impossible situation — can loom like giants. God does not ask us to pretend they are small. He asks us to remember what He has already done, supremely at the cross and empty tomb. The God who conquered sin and death for us is more than able to carry us through whatever we face (Rom 8:31-32). When fear says "too big," faith answers, "remember well what the Lord has done." Look at your God, not just your giants.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- What "giants" am I staring at that make me afraid?
- How can remembering God's past faithfulness fuel my courage now?
- What has God already done for me that assures me He will carry me through?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, when fear whispers that my problems are too big, help me remember how great You are. You conquered sin and death for me — surely You will carry me through. Fix my eyes on You, not on my giants. Amen.
